audio_content_summary: John Mearsheimer (University of Chicago political scientist) argues the U.S. is 'an incredibly ruthless country,' citing the 2025 Lancet Global Health sanctions-mortality study — sanctions 1971–2021, which he summarizes as '38 million people' killed — then characterizes U.S. economic pressure on Venezuela, Cuba and Iran as deliberately starving populations to provoke uprisings, and concludes he finds it hard to call the U.S. a noble or exceptionally virtuous country in foreign policy.
implied_frame: Group A (verifiable): the Lancet Global Health study exists and its estimates imply ~38 million deaths associated with US/EU unilateral sanctions over 1971–2021 — covered by record 2025-sanctions-mortality-lancet-001. Group B (framing/slips): Mearsheimer says the study came out 'November of 2025' (published online July 2025); calls it 'American sanctions' (the study covers US or EU sanctions, strongest effects for US ones); and renders the study's statistical association as 'we murdered' — the study reports association, not adjudicated intent. His reading of sanctions policy as deliberately starving Venezuelans/Cubans/Iranians to trigger uprisings is his characterization, attributable to him.
